title: How to Build a Glean Workflow
summary: A Glean workflow connects internal data sources to external tools to trigger automated actions. You can evaluate if this integration fits your stack.
body_markdown:
## Automating Glean actions with Activepieces workflows


Activepieces puts every Glean-triggered agent inside the same access model as your employees: RBAC, SSO, and SCIM govern what it may connect to, not just what a person may open.


An SDK gives a Glean agent code to run, but it does not provide the tenant-wide audit log or role-based access required for enterprise governance.


Activepieces places every agent under the same access policies as your employees, ensuring it can only connect to authorized data sources.


You can open the run detail view for any agent step to verify that each tool call is logged individually with its specific input and output, rather than being collapsed into an opaque result.


### Link search events to your workflow


You link Glean to Activepieces by configuring a Webhook trigger that listens for the Search API’s event payloads, which can then be processed by any of the 750 integrations available in the open source monorepo.


Because Activepieces provides a dedicated URL for its webhook listener, you can paste this directly into the Glean administrator console to begin automating with the MIT-licensed core.


Once the connection is live, a test run in the Activepieces builder displays the JSON structure of your Glean data, allowing you to map fields like "Document Title" to subsequent steps without writing code.


Every connector registered in Activepieces is immediately available as an agent tool. Once an integration is configured, it runs as a step in a flow and as a tool schema on a per-project MCP server, reachable from an agent you built or external models.


You can verify this in the Integrations Framework and MCP Server documentation, where the same integration action in the open-source repository is exposed as a reusable tool without a second migration.


### Building a multi-step logic branch for search results


To handle complex enterprise routing, you use the "Branch" integration in Activepieces to sort Glean results based on their source or content type.


Destination Logic Condition


Salesforce If the Glean result originates from a "Customer Success" folder, the workflow creates a Task in the Salesforce CRM.


Jira If the result contains technical keywords or bug report metadata, Activepieces opens a new Issue in the relevant Jira project.


Webhook For any results that do not fit standard categories, the workflow sends the raw data to a generic Webhook.


### Deploying the workflow to production teams


Moving a workflow from the builder to the team requires assigning a specific "Worker Identity" to the Activepieces connection to maintain a clear audit trail. This ensures that when a Jira ticket is created, the "Created By" field shows the AI agent's name.


You then publish the flow using the "Production" toggle. By monitoring the "Runs" tab, you can verify every execution and re-run any failed steps if a destination service is temporarily unreachable.
